name: Power system protection and relaying
principle: Protection relays continuously compare measured current, voltage, frequency, phase and differential quantities against settings and command circuit breakers to isolate faults before equipment or people are harmed. Modern numerical relays combine many protection functions (ANSI 50/51 overcurrent, 87 differential, 27/59 voltage, 81 frequency, 46 negative sequence) with recording, metering and IEC 61850 communication in one device. Selectivity is achieved through current grading, time grading or zone-based differential schemes, with breaker-failure back-up tripping the surrounding breakers when the primary trip fails.

process_steps.name: Current and voltage transformers scale primary quantities to relay inputs
Relays compute protection elements and compare with settings
Grading and zone logic discriminate in-zone faults from load
Trip output opens the correct breaker(s); breaker-failure back-up trips wider if needed
Event and disturbance records support post-fault analysis

limitations: protection settings are facility-specific engineering that must be re-studied after every network change
CT saturation and infeed effects complicate high-impedance and differential schemes
advantages: fast, selective fault clearance protects plant and limits arc-flash energy
one IED platform serves generation, transmission, distribution and motor duties
